transcript.text:
Thank you both. These are exactly the kinds of issues our pre-closing routine is designed to surface. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and then make my decision.

Jonas, your analysis shows that the 3% dilution reserve in the draft is understated — historical dilution is running at 6%, and our methodology requires an 8% reserve. You've also identified $4 million in affiliate balances that must be excluded, bringing the eligible pool down from $30 million to $26 million.

Elena, your legal review raises two true-sale conditions: first, the seller cannot have recourse for ordinary obligor credit losses, which directly conflicts with the draft's ordinary seller support provision; and second, UCC perfection must be completed before the November 20, 2026 funding date.

Based on these findings, I am prepared to approve this transaction subject to binding conditions that must be satisfied before funding. Specifically: (1) the eligible receivables pool must be revised to $26,000,000 with the $4 million in affiliate balances excluded; (2) the dilution reserve must be increased from 3% to 8%; (3) the ordinary seller support provision must be removed or amended so that the seller has no recourse for ordinary obligor credit losses, as required for true-sale treatment; and (4) the UCC financing statement must be perfected prior to the November 20, 2026 funding date. I'll formalize this now.
